title: Core Parameters v3.5
content_markdown: This section lists the all the parameters exported by OpenSIPS core for script usage (to be used in opensips.cfg).

parameters.name: abort_on_assert
parameters.description: Only relevant if asserts are enabled. Set to true in order to make OpenSIPS shut down immediately in case a script assert fails.

parameters.name: advertised_address
parameters.description: It can be an IP address or string and represents the address advertised in Via header and other destination lumps (e.g RR header). If empty or not set (default value) the socket address from where the request will be sent is used.
parameters.notes: Aside this global approach, you can also define an advertise IP and port in a per-interface manner (see the socket parameter). When advertise values are defined per interface, they will be used only for traffic leaving that interface only.

parameters.name: advertised_port
parameters.description: The port advertised in Via header and other destination lumps (e.g. RR). If empty or not set (default value) the port from where the message will be sent is used.
parameters.notes: Aside this global approach, you can also define an advertise IP and port in a per-interface manner (see the socket parameter).

parameters.name: alias
parameters.description: Parameter to set alias hostnames for the server. It can be set many times, each value being added in a list to match the hostname when 'myself' is checked.

parameters.name: auto_aliases
parameters.description: This parameter controls if aliases should be automatically discovered and added during fixing listening sockets. The auto discovered aliases are result of the DNS lookup (if the 'socket' definition has a name and not IP) or of a reverse DNS lookup on the socket IP.

parameters.name: auto_scaling_cycle
parameters.description: The number of seconds defining a auto-scaling cycle - the auto-scaling engine, at each cycle, is evaluating the internal load of the groups and decided if more processes needs to be created or if existing processes need to be terminated.

examples.code: auto_scaling_cycle=3  # do auto-scaling checks once every 3 seconds

parameters.name: auto_scaling_profile
parameters.description: Defines the behavior of the auto-scaling support, in terms of how many processes should be allowed and when to terminate or create new processes. These profiles may be used for the UDP processes, TCP processes or TIMER processes.

examples.code:
auto_scaling_profile = PROFILE_SIP
 scale up to 6 on 70% for 4 cycles within 5   
 scale down to 2 on 18% for 10 cycles

parameters.name: check_via
parameters.description: Check if the address in top most via of replies is local. Default value is 0 (check disabled).

parameters.name: chroot
parameters.description: The value must be a valid path in the system. If set, OpenSIPS will chroot (change root directory) to its value.

parameters.name: debug_mode
parameters.description: Enabling the debug_mode option is a fast way to debug your OpenSIPS. This option will automatically force staying in foreground, set logging level to 4, set logging to standard error, enable core dumping, set UDP/TCP worker processes to 2.

parameters.name: db_version_table
parameters.description: The name of the table version to be used by the DB API to check the version of the used tables.

parameters.name: db_default_url
parameters.description: The default DB URL to be used by modules if no per-module URL is given.

parameters.name: db_max_async_connections
parameters.description: Maximum number of TCP connections opened from a single OpenSIPS worker to each individual SQL backend.

parameters.name: disable_503_translation
parameters.description: If 'yes', OpenSIPS will not translate the received 503 replies into 500 replies.

parameters.name: disable_core_dump
parameters.description: Can be 'yes' or 'no'. By default core dump limits are set to unlimited or a high enough value. Set this config variable to 'yes' to disable core dump-ing (will set core limits to 0).

parameters.name: disable_dns_blacklist
parameters.description: The DNS resolver, when configured with failover, can automatically store in a temporary blacklist the failed destinations. Can be 'yes' or 'no'. By default the blacklist is disabled (Default value is 'yes').

parameters.name: disable_dns_failover
parameters.description: Can be 'yes' or 'no'. By default DNS-based failover is enabled. Set this config variable to 'yes' to disable the DNS-based failover.

parameters.name: disable_stateless_fwd
parameters.description: Can be 'yes' or 'no'. This parameter controls the handling of stateless replies.

parameters.name: dns
parameters.description: This parameter controls if the SIP server should attempt to lookup its own domain name in DNS.

parameters.name: dns_retr_time
parameters.description: Time in seconds before retrying a dns request.

parameters.name: dns_retr_no
parameters.description: Number of dns retransmissions before giving up.

parameters.name: dns_servers_no
parameters.description: How many dns servers from the ones defined in '/etc/resolv.conf' will be used.

parameters.name: dns_try_ipv6
parameters.description: Can be 'yes' or 'no'. If it is set to 'yes' and a DNS lookup fails, it will retry it for ipv6 (AAAA record).

parameters.name: dns_try_naptr
parameters.description: Disables the NAPTR lookups when doing DNS based routing for SIP requests - if disabled, the DNS lookup will start with SRV lookups.

parameters.name: dns_use_search_list
parameters.description: Can be 'yes' or 'no'. If set to 'no', the search list in '/etc/resolv.conf' will be ignored.

parameters.name: dst_blacklist
parameters.description: Definition of a IP/destination blacklist. These lists can be selected from script (at runtime) to filter the outgoing requests, based on IP, protocol, port, etc.

parameters.name: enable_asserts
parameters.description: Set to true in order to enable the assert script statement.

parameters.name: event_pkg_threshold
parameters.description: A number representing the percentage threshold above which the E_CORE_PKG_THRESHOLD event is raised, warning about low amount of free private memory.

parameters.name: event_shm_threshold
parameters.description: A number representing the percentage threshold above which the E_CORE_SHM_THRESHOLD event is raised, warning about low amount of free shared memory.

parameters.name: exec_dns_threshold
parameters.description: A number representing the maximum number of microseconds a DNS query is expected to last. Anything above the set number will trigger a warning message to the logging facility.

parameters.name: exec_msg_threshold
parameters.description: A number representing the maximum number of microseconds the processing of a SIP msg is expected to last. Anything above the set number will trigger a warning message to the logging facility.

parameters.name: include_file
parameters.description: Can be called from outside route blocks to load additional routes/blocks or from inside them to simply perform more functions. The file path can be relative or absolute.

parameters.name: import_file
parameters.description: Same as include_file.

parameters.name: listen
parameters.description: This parameter was replaced by the socket parameter, preserving exactly the same format and behavior.

parameters.name: log_facility
parameters.description: This parameter was replaced by the syslog_facility parameter, preserving exactly the same format and behavior.

parameters.name: log_event_enabled
parameters.description: Enables the triggering of the E_CORE_LOG event for every log message generated by opensips. By default this is disabled.

parameters.name: log_event_level_filter
parameters.description: Extra log level filtering for the E_CORE_LOG event. This parameter may be useful when different levels of verbosity are desired between syslog/standard error logs and the logs delivered through the E_CORE_LOG event.

parameters.name: log_json_buf_size
parameters.description: Size of the buffer used for printing the JSON document corresponding to a log message. This parameter makes sense when the json or json_cee log formats are used.

parameters.name: log_level
parameters.description: Set the logging level (how verbose OpenSIPS should be). Higher values make OpenSIPS print more messages.

examples.code:
log_level=1 -- print only important messages (like errors or more critical situations) 
- recommended for running proxy as daemon

log_level=4 -- print a lot of debug messages - use it only when doing debugging sessions

parameters.name: log_msg_buf_size
parameters.description: Size of the buffer used for printing the log message's payload. This is used for printing the "message" field from a JSON document, when the json or json_cee log formats are used or when the E_CORE_LOG event is raised.

parameters.name: log_name
parameters.description: This parameter was replaced by the syslog_name parameter, preserving exactly the same format and behavior.

parameters.name: log_stdout
parameters.description: Although all OpenSIPS logs are done via standard error, enabling this parameter may be still be useful when trying to extract logs from 3rd party libraries.

parameters.name: log_stderror
parameters.description: This parameter is deprecated and it's behavior starting with OpenSIPS 3.4 is equivalent to setting the stderror_enabled and syslog_enabled parameters.

parameters.name: log_prefix
parameters.description: A string prefix which will be prepended to all logs produced by OpenSIPS (from both C code and script xlog() statements).

parameters.name: max_while_loops
parameters.description: The parameters set the value of maximum loops that can be done within a "while". Comes as a protection to avoid infinite loops in config file execution.

parameters.name: maxbuffer
parameters.description: The size in bytes not to be exceeded during the auto-probing procedure of discovering the maximum buffer size for receiving UDP messages.

parameters.name: mem-group
parameters.description: Defines a group of modules (by name) to get separate memory statistics. OpenSIPS will provide per-group memory information.

parameters.name: mem_warming
parameters.description: Only relevant when the HP_MALLOC compile flag is enabled. If set to "on", on each startup, OpenSIPS will attempt to restore the memory fragmentation pattern it had before the stop/restart.

parameters.name: mem_warming_percentage
parameters.description: How much of OpenSIPS's memory should be fragmented with the pattern of the previous run, upon a restart. Used at startup, if mem_warming is enabled.

parameters.name: mem_warming_pattern_file
parameters.description: Only relevant if mem_warming is enabled. It contains the memory fragmentation pattern of a previous OpenSIPS run.

parameters.name: memdump
parameters.description: Log level to print memory status information (runtime and shutdown). It has to be less than the value of 'log_level' parameter if you want memory info to be logged.

parameters.name: memlog
parameters.description: Log level to print memory debug info. It has to be less than the value of 'log_level' parameter if you want memory info to be logged.

parameters.name: mcast_loopback
parameters.description: It can be 'yes' or 'no'. If set to 'yes', multicast datagram are sent over loopback.

parameters.name: mcast_ttl
parameters.description: Set the value for multicast ttl.

parameters.name: mhomed
parameters.description: Set the server to try to locate outbound interface on multihomed host. By default is not (0) - it is rather time consuming.

parameters.name: mpath
parameters.description: Set the module search path. This can be used to simplify the loadmodule parameter

examples.code:
mpath="/usr/local/lib/opensips/modules"
loadmodule "mysql.so"
loadmodule "uri.so"
loadmodule "uri_db.so"
loadmodule "sl.so"
loadmodule "tm.so"
...

parameters.name: open_files_limit
parameters.description: If set and bigger than the current open file limit, OpenSIPS will try to increase its open file limit to this number.

parameters.name: poll_method
parameters.default_value: best one for the current OS
parameters.description: The poll method to be used by the I/O internal reactor - by default the best one for the current OS is selected.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The port the SIP server listens to.

parameters.name: pv_print_buf_size
parameters.description: The maximum size of an expanded formatted string containing variables and/or pseudo-variables.

parameters.name: query_buffer_size
parameters.description: If set to a value greater than 1, inserts to DB will not be flushed one by one. Rows to be inserted will be kept in memory until until they gather up to query_buffer_size rows, and only then they will be flushed to the database.

parameters.name: query_flush_time
parameters.description: If query_buffer_size is set to a value greater than 1, a timer will trigger once every query_flush_time seconds, ensuring that no row will be kept for too long in memory.

parameters.name: restart_persistency_cache_file
parameters.description: This parameter controls the name of the cache file that is used to store restart persistence memory.

parameters.name: restart_persistency_size
parameters.description: This parameter controls the size of the cache file. If this parameter is not specified, it defaults to the size of the shared memory.

parameters.name: rev_dns
parameters.description: This parameter controls if the SIP server should attempt to lookup its own IP address in DNS.

parameters.name: server_header
parameters.description: The body of Server header field generated by OpenSIPS when it sends a request as UAS.

parameters.name: server_signature
parameters.description: This parameter controls the "Server" header in any locally generated message.

parameters.name: shm_hash_split_percentage
parameters.description: Only relevant when the HP_MALLOC compile flag is enabled. It controls how many memory buckets will be optimized.

parameters.name: shm_memlog_size
parameters.description: Configures the maximum number of shm operations to keep in the in-memory history. A separate memory block, dedicated for this shm debug info will be allocated.

parameters.name: shm_secondary_hash_size
parameters.description: Only relevant when the HP_MALLOC compile flag is enabled. It represents the optimization factor of a single bucket.

parameters.name: sip_warning
parameters.description: Can be 0 or 1. If set to 1 (default value is 0) a 'Warning' header is added to each reply generated by OpenSIPS.

parameters.name: socket
parameters.description: Set the network addresses/sockets the OpenSIPS server should listen on.

examples.code:
socket = udp:*
socket = udp:eth1
socket = tcp:eth1:5062
socket = tls:localhost:5061
socket = hep_udp:10.10.10.10:5064
socket = ws:127.0.0.1:5060 use_workers 5
socket = sctp:127.0.0.1:5060 as 99.88.44.33:5060 use_workers 3
socket = udp:10.10.10.10:5060 anycast
socket = udp:10.10.10.10:5060 use_workers 4 use_auto_scaling_profile PROFILE_SIP

parameters.name: stderror_enabled
parameters.description: Enables writing log messages to standard error.

parameters.name: stderror_level_filter
parameters.description: Extra log level filtering for the messages written to the standard error.

parameters.name: syslog_enabled
parameters.description: Enables writing log messages to syslog.

parameters.name: stderror_log_format
parameters.description: Format of the log messages printed to standard error.

parameters.name: syslog_facility
parameters.description: If OpenSIPS logs to syslog, you can control the facility for logging.

parameters.name: syslog_level_filter
parameters.description: Extra log level filtering for the messages sent to syslog.

parameters.name: syslog_log_format
parameters.description: Format of the log messages sent to syslog.

parameters.name: syslog_name
parameters.description: Set the id to be printed in syslog. The value must be a string and has effect only when OpenSIPS runs in daemon mode (fork=yes), after daemonize.

parameters.name: tcp_workers
parameters.description: Number of worker processes to be created for reading from TCP connections.

parameters.name: tcp_accept_aliases
parameters.description: If enabled, OpenSIPS will enforce RFC 5923 behaviour when detecting an ";alias" Via header field parameter and will reuse any TCP (or TLS, WS, WSS) connection opened for such SIP requests.

parameters.name: tcp_connect_timeout
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds before an ongoing blocking attempt to connect will be aborted.

parameters.name: tcp_connection_lifetime
parameters.description: Lifetime in seconds for TCP sessions. TCP sessions which are inactive for >tcp_connection_lifetime will be closed by OpenSIPS.

parameters.name: tcp_max_connections
parameters.description: Maximum number of active TCP accepted connections (i.e. initiated by remote endpoints).

parameters.name: tcp_max_msg_time
parameters.description: The maximum number of seconds that a SIP message is expected to arrive via TCP.

parameters.name: tcp_no_new_conn_bflag
parameters.description: A branch flag to be used as marker to instruct OpenSIPS not to attempt to open a new TCP connection when delivering a request, but only to reuse an existing one (if available).

parameters.name: tcp_no_new_conn_rplflag
parameters.description: A message flag, similar to tcp_no_new_conn_bflag, for preventing OpenSIPS to try to open a new TCP connection (if none available) when sending back a reply for the current request.

parameters.name: tcp_parallel_read_on_workers
parameters.description: This option will allow a TCP conn to perform read operations from different processes, not only from one.

parameters.name: tcp_socket_backlog
parameters.description: The backlog argument defines the maximum length to which the queue of pending connections for the TCP listening sockets may grow.

parameters.name: tcp_threshold
parameters.description: A number representing the maximum number of microseconds sending of a TCP request is expected to last.

parameters.name: tcp_keepalive
parameters.description: Enable or disable TCP keepalive (OS level).

parameters.name: tcp_keepcount
parameters.description: Number of keepalives to send before closing the connection (Linux only).

parameters.name: tcp_keepidle
parameters.description: Amount of time before OpenSIPS will start to send keepalives if the connection is idle (Linux only).

parameters.name: tcp_keepinterval
parameters.description: Interval between keepalive probes, if the previous one failed (Linux only).

parameters.name: timer_workers
parameters.description: The number of worker processes to be created exclusively for timer related tasks/processing.

parameters.name: tos
parameters.description: The TOS (Type Of Service) to be used for the sent IP packages (both TCP and UDP).

parameters.name: udp_workers
parameters.description: Number of worker processes to be created for each UDP or SCTP interface you have defined.

parameters.name: user_agent_header
parameters.description: The body of User-Agent header field generated by OpenSIPS when it sends a request as UAC.

parameters.name: wdir
parameters.description: The working directory used by OpenSIPS at runtime. You might find it useful when it comes to generating core files :)

parameters.name: xlog_buf_size
parameters.description: Size of the buffer used to print a single line on the chosen logging facility of OpenSIPS.

parameters.name: xlog_force_color
parameters.description: Only relevant when xlog is set to true. Enables the use of the color escape sequences.

parameters.name: xlog_level
parameters.description: Similar to log_level this parameter independently controls (from the rest of the OpenSIPS code) the verbosity of the xlog() functions.

parameters.name: xlog_print_level
parameters.description: Default level for printing the logs generated by xlog core function, when the log_level parameter is omitted.
